rule.title: Visa Fraud Monitoring Program
rule.note: This reason code generally cannot be represented. Recommend accepting liability unless the merchant can prove the transaction was miscoded by the issuer.

summary.allegation: The issuer has charged back the transaction under the Visa Fraud Monitoring Program, asserting that this transaction was identified as fraudulent within that programme rather than disputing the individual merits of the sale.
summary.to_defend: Visa allows a representment for 10.5 only where the merchant can show the transaction was miscoded by the issuer under the Fraud Monitoring Program.

requirements.title: Proof the issuer miscoded the chargeback
requirements.text: Evidence that the transaction was miscoded by the issuer under the Visa Fraud Monitoring Program.
requirements.finding: Nothing supplied addresses issuer miscoding under the Visa Fraud Monitoring Program. The two documents go to the merits of the sale (Visa Secure authentication and a delivery confirmation), which is not the exception this reason code allows.
requirements.gap: No evidence that the issuer wrongly coded or reported this transaction under the Fraud Monitoring Program, for example Visa programme correspondence, a VFMP notification listing showing the transaction in error, or acquirer confirmation that the fraud report was withdrawn.

documents.label: Visa Secure authentication record
documents.reason: Shows successful 3DS authentication for txn_1178ST, which goes to the merits of the fraud claim and does not evidence issuer miscoding under the Fraud Monitoring Program.

documents.label: Order delivery confirmation, Evri tracking
documents.reason: Confirms delivery of order BB-77231, which is merits evidence and does not address the only defence available under 10.5.

alerts.text: Visa 10.5 generally cannot be represented. The evidence is shown but does not change the outcome unless it proves miscoding.

justification: Accept liability: R1 is missing, as no evidence shows the issuer miscoded the transaction under the Visa Fraud Monitoring Program, the only defence permitted for reason code 10.5.
rationale:
The chargeback is filed under Visa reason code 10.5, which may only be represented where the issuer miscoded the transaction under the Visa Fraud Monitoring Program.
The merchant has supplied a Visa Secure authentication record and an Evri delivery confirmation for order BB-77231, both of which address the merits of the sale rather than programme coding.
No Visa Fraud Monitoring Program correspondence or acquirer confirmation has been produced to show the transaction was reported or coded in error.
With the sole permitted defence unsupported, liability for the 78.50 GBP transaction of 30 April 2025 is accepted.
analyst_notes: Strong merits evidence exists (3DS authenticated, ECI 05, AVS Y, CVV M, delivery to billing postcode SW4 7QR); worth raising with the acquirer whether the issuer should have filed under a different code or whether the fraud report can be withdrawn.
Confirm with the merchant whether they have received any VFMP or acquirer fraud monitoring notifications covering April 2025 before closing the case.
